test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Mechanic Motor Vehicle) Official Paper (Held On: 06 May, 2025 Shift 1)
subject: general
question: What is the primary reason for the heating effect in a conductor when an electric current passes through it?

options.text: The electric field in the conductor causes heat generation.
The movement of protons causes heat generation
The conductor absorbs heat from the surrounding environment.
The movement of electrons causes heat generation.

solution:
The correct answer is __The movement of electrons causes heat generation**(Option 4)**.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The movement of electrons__ is the primary reason for the heating effect in a conductor when an electric current passes through it.
 
• Electrons collide with atoms in the conductor, transferring their kinetic energy, which results in heat generation.
 
• This phenomenon is known as Joule heating or resistive heating.
 
• It occurs because of the resistance of the conductor to the flow of electric current.
 
• Joule's law states that the heat produced is proportional to the square of the current, the resistance, and the time the current is applied.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Electric Field:**
 
 
• The electric field does not directly cause heat generation but facilitates the movement of electrons.
 
• It is the collisions of electrons with atoms that lead to heat generation.
 
 
 
• **Protons:**
 
 
• Protons are stationary in the nucleus of atoms and do not contribute to the flow of current or heat generation.
 
• The movement of electrons is responsible for the heating effect, not protons.
 
 
 
• **Surrounding Environment:**
 
 
• Heat is not absorbed from the surrounding environment but is generated within the conductor due to resistive heating.
